chunks: From him, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Abu Al-Hasan Al-Rida (peace be upon him), that he
would sprinkle dust upon the letter (to dry the ink), and said: 'There is no problem with it'.

key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ بِهِ: there is no problem with it

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to use dust to dry ink on letters in Islam?
ai.summary: This hadith from Imam Al-Rida (peace be upon him) establishes the permissibility of using dust to dry ink on written letters, reflecting the practical administrative norms of the early Islamic period. It serves as a legal ruling confirming that this action does not invalidate the writing or constitute a ritual impurity issue in this context, emphasizing the flexibility of fiqh in daily affairs.

en.hubeali: From him, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Abu Nasr,
(It has been narrated) from Abu Al-Hassan Al-Reza<sup>asws</sup> that he<sup>asws</sup> would (sprinkle) dust upon the letter (to dry the ink), and said: ‘There is no problem with it’.
en.sarwar: 8. It is narrated from him (narrator of the Hadith above) from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn abu Nasr who has said the following: “Abu al-Hassan al-Rida (a.s.)
would dry up the ink on a newlywritten letter by means of placing soil on it and would say that doing so is not an offense.”
